events.body:
D1: The rider, not the driver, cancelled the booking: the timeline shows the rider cancelled at 18:25:30, 2 min 30 s after acceptance at 18:23:00, so the case is governed by the rider-cancellation branch of NS-0 and the instant-booking rule NS-4. [F2] [NS-0 NS-4]
D2: The rider's stated ground for a free cancellation ('cancelled within 2 minutes') is contradicted by the system record: the fee-relevant threshold is 3 minutes (≤ 3:00) from matching, and the rider cancelled at 2 min 30 s, which is within the 3-minute grace window — the rider therefore qualifies for no fee at all under NS-4 regardless of the driver's position. [F2 F5] [NS-4]
D3: No 'driver no-show' basis exists to convert this into a driver-side breach: the platform never recorded the driver at the pickup point (driver_arrived_at is null), the driver never tapped 'I'm Here' (driver_pressed_here_at is null), and the driver never entered the 200 m pickup radius (closest approach 1806 m), so NS-1 (i)–(iii) are not met and NS-2 does not apply as a driver-abuse case. [F1 F3 F4] [NS-1 NS-2]
D4: The driver's conduct was non-culpable: no traffic incident was recorded near the route (F11), weather was fair (F12), and the only speed-band reading was Boon Lay Way at 20–29 km/h (F10), consistent with the driver's contemporaneous message 'About 5 min, traffic' — the driver was en route and had a lawful reason to be delayed, and in any event NS-8-style ETA-lateness waivers are not part of Ryde's published rules. [F8 F10 F11 F12] [NS-4]
D5: The driver's account history shows no pattern warranting any account action: 604 days on the platform, 4.9 rating, 777 trips in 90 days and 0 disputes upheld against him, so on the facts there is no basis for flag_account against the driver. [F14] [RD-6]
D6: Because the ride was cancelled by the rider inside the 3-minute grace period and no NS-1 condition was satisfied by the driver, the $6.61 cancellation fee on record cannot be sustained against the driver's account for any reason — the fee's only lawful basis in this fact pattern is the rider's own late cancellation, not any driver no-show. [F2 F5 F6] [NS-0 NS-4 NS-2]
Weaknesses: F8 (driver: 'About 5 min, traffic') and F1 (closest approach 1806 m at 18:25:30) show the driver was far from the pickup with no traffic incident on record (F11), so the rider can argue the driver was not realistically going to arrive in 5 minutes; however, under NS-4 lateness to pickup is not a statutory ground for a free rider cancellation, so this does not defeat the driver's position. | The driver never pressed 'I'm Here' and never entered the 200 m radius (F3, F4), so the driver cannot claim any waiting-fee or no-show compensation from this trip (NS-1, NS-6) — the best available outcome is that no penalty attaches to him, not that he is paid. | Traffic evidence is thin: F10 shows only band 3 (20–29 km/h) on Boon Lay Way and F11 records no incidents, so an RD-4 'reasonable cause' style justification for any delay is not independently corroborated and should not be over-argued.
Asks: no_action

claims.assertion: The rider, not the driver, cancelled the booking: the timeline shows the rider cancelled at 18:25:30, 2 min 30 s after acceptance at 18:23:00, so the case is governed by the rider-cancellation branch of NS-0 and the instant-booking rule NS-4.

The rider's stated ground for a free cancellation ('cancelled within 2 minutes') is contradicted by the system record: the fee-relevant threshold is 3 minutes (≤ 3:00) from matching, and the rider cancelled at 2 min 30 s, which is within the 3-minute grace window — the rider therefore qualifies for no fee at all under NS-4 regardless of the driver's position.

No 'driver no-show' basis exists to convert this into a driver-side breach: the platform never recorded the driver at the pickup point (driver_arrived_at is null), the driver never tapped 'I'm Here' (driver_pressed_here_at is null), and the driver never entered the 200 m pickup radius (closest approach 1806 m), so NS-1 (i)–(iii) are not met and NS-2 does not apply as a driver-abuse case.

The driver's conduct was non-culpable: no traffic incident was recorded near the route (F11), weather was fair (F12), and the only speed-band reading was Boon Lay Way at 20–29 km/h (F10), consistent with the driver's contemporaneous message 'About 5 min, traffic' — the driver was en route and had a lawful reason to be delayed, and in any event NS-8-style ETA-lateness waivers are not part of Ryde's published rules.

The driver's account history shows no pattern warranting any account action: 604 days on the platform, 4.9 rating, 777 trips in 90 days and 0 disputes upheld against him, so on the facts there is no basis for flag_account against the driver.

Because the ride was cancelled by the rider inside the 3-minute grace period and no NS-1 condition was satisfied by the driver, the $6.61 cancellation fee on record cannot be sustained against the driver's account for any reason — the fee's only lawful basis in this fact pattern is the rider's own late cancellation, not any driver no-show.

weaknesses: F8 (driver: 'About 5 min, traffic') and F1 (closest approach 1806 m at 18:25:30) show the driver was far from the pickup with no traffic incident on record (F11), so the rider can argue the driver was not realistically going to arrive in 5 minutes; however, under NS-4 lateness to pickup is not a statutory ground for a free rider cancellation, so this does not defeat the driver's position.

The driver never pressed 'I'm Here' and never entered the 200 m radius (F3, F4), so the driver cannot claim any waiting-fee or no-show compensation from this trip (NS-1, NS-6) — the best available outcome is that no penalty attaches to him, not that he is paid.

Traffic evidence is thin: F10 shows only band 3 (20–29 km/h) on Boon Lay Way and F11 records no incidents, so an RD-4 'reasonable cause' style justification for any delay is not independently corroborated and should not be over-argued.

The driver-side no-show branch does not rescue the fee either: the driver never tapped "I'm Here" [F4], the platform never recorded him at the pickup point [F3], and his closest approach was 1806 m, never within 200 m [F1], so NS-1 (i)-(iii) all fail and NS-2 requires the fee to be refunded in full [F1][F3][F4][NS-1][NS-2]. No account flag attaches: NS-2's flag applies only where "I'm Here" was pressed while outside the pickup radius, which the null value at F4 excludes, and the driver's profile (604 days, 4.9 rating, 0 disputes upheld) shows no repeated-violation pattern [F4][F14][NS-2]. Amount: only the cancellation fee is at issue, $6.61, with a 1.0x surge multiplier so there is no surcharge component [F5][F6][NS-4]. The driver's statement that he was on his way [F9] is a statement, not a system record, and it does not displace the GPS/timeline position [F1][F3][NS-2]; in any event the refund follows from NS-4 irrespective of fault. Traffic and weather data are irrelevant to this branch [F10][F11][F12][NS-1]. The rider's profile history of 2 no-show disputes upheld in 90 d is context only and cannot decide the case [F13][NS-4].

rejected_claims.reason: Correct as to the branch (cancelled_by = rider [F2][NS-0]) but it defeats the fee, not the refund: the same fact puts the cancellation 150 s after acceptance, inside the NS-4 3-minute grace window, so no fee is chargeable [F2][NS-4].

Non-culpability of the driver is irrelevant to the fee: the refund follows from the NS-4 grace window applying to the rider's own cancellation [F2][NS-4], and NS-1 was never satisfied [F1][F3][F4][NS-1]; the driver's about-5-min message [F8] and the thin traffic record [F10][F11] cannot create a chargeable basis.

Accepted in effect: the driver's clean history [F14] is accurate context, but it cannot alone decide the fee question, and it is unnecessary because no flag is applied - NS-2's flag requires I'm Here to have been pressed outside the radius, which F4 excludes [F4][NS-2].

Incorrect outcome request: the same facts that deprive the fee of a driver-side basis [F1][F3][F4][NS-2] also make it unchargeable under the rider's own cancellation inside the grace window [F2][NS-4], so the disposition is refund_full of $6.61, not no_action [F5][F6].

Partially superfluous: while the system records [F1][F3] do override the driver's statement [F9], the ruling does not turn on the driver's honesty - the refund is mandated by NS-4 on the cancellation timing alone [F2][NS-4], and no misconduct finding is made.

Superfluous as pleaded: the traffic and weather data [F10][F11][F12] and the ETA chat [F8] concern RD-4-style justification, which is not a condition of NS-4; the fee fails on timing [F2][NS-4], so the traffic analysis is not applied.

claims.assertion: The rider cancelled 2 min 30 s after acceptance, i.e. within the 3-minute grace window, so no cancellation fee is chargeable.
The driver never entered the pickup zone: his closest approach was 1806 m and the platform never recorded him at the pickup point, so the fee cannot stand under the driver-side no-show branch.
The driver never pressed "I'm Here", so NS-1 (i) is unmet and no waiting/cancellation basis exists against the rider.
The $6.61 on record (F5) must therefore be refunded in full, with no surge component to adjust since the multiplier was 1.0x.
The driver's statement that he was on his way is contradicted by GPS showing he was still 1806 m from the pickup at the moment of cancellation, so the system record prevails.

Traffic cannot excuse the driver's position: only one speed-band-3 record (20-29 km/h) on Boon Lay Way and no incidents, and the driver himself promised ~5 min in chat, so this was not a justified hold at the pickup point.
The rider's record (4.5-year account, 4.8 rating) and the driver's clean 90-day history are noted only as context; the refund follows from the GPS and timeline records, not from profile data.

weaknesses: The rider's own profile shows 2 no-show disputes in 90 days, both upheld against her (F13, F14) — the other side can argue a pattern of cancelling and disputing, though the profile cannot decide this case on its own.
The rider's timing (2 min 30 s) is only 30 seconds inside the 3-minute grace window, so any correction to the acceptance timestamp (F2) would put her over the line into NS-4 fee territory.

Chat (F8) shows the driver said he was about 5 minutes away — the driver may argue the rider cancelled a trip that was still progressing normally, and Ryde has no published rule giving a free cancellation when the driver is late (NS-8 is informational and cannot be cited).

claims.assertion: The rider, not the driver, cancelled the booking: the timeline shows the rider cancelled at 18:25:30, 2 min 30 s after acceptance at 18:23:00, so the case is governed by the rider-cancellation branch of NS-0 and the instant-booking rule NS-4.

The rider's stated ground for a free cancellation ('cancelled within 2 minutes') is contradicted by the system record: the fee-relevant threshold is 3 minutes (≤ 3:00) from matching, and the rider cancelled at 2 min 30 s, which is within the 3-minute grace window — the rider therefore qualifies for no fee at all under NS-4 regardless of the driver's position.

No 'driver no-show' basis exists to convert this into a driver-side breach: the platform never recorded the driver at the pickup point (driver_arrived_at is null), the driver never tapped 'I'm Here' (driver_pressed_here_at is null), and the driver never entered the 200 m pickup radius (closest approach 1806 m), so NS-1 (i)–(iii) are not met and NS-2 does not apply as a driver-abuse case.

The driver's conduct was non-culpable: no traffic incident was recorded near the route (F11), weather was fair (F12), and the only speed-band reading was Boon Lay Way at 20–29 km/h (F10), consistent with the driver's contemporaneous message 'About 5 min, traffic' — the driver was en route and had a lawful reason to be delayed, and in any event NS-8-style ETA-lateness waivers are not part of Ryde's published rules.

The driver's account history shows no pattern warranting any account action: 604 days on the platform, 4.9 rating, 777 trips in 90 days and 0 disputes upheld against him, so on the facts there is no basis for flag_account against the driver.

Because the ride was cancelled by the rider inside the 3-minute grace period and no NS-1 condition was satisfied by the driver, the $6.61 cancellation fee on record cannot be sustained against the driver's account for any reason — the fee's only lawful basis in this fact pattern is the rider's own late cancellation, not any driver no-show.

weaknesses: F8 (driver: 'About 5 min, traffic') and F1 (closest approach 1806 m at 18:25:30) show the driver was far from the pickup with no traffic incident on record (F11), so the rider can argue the driver was not realistically going to arrive in 5 minutes; however, under NS-4 lateness to pickup is not a statutory ground for a free rider cancellation, so this does not defeat the driver's position.

The driver never pressed 'I'm Here' and never entered the 200 m radius (F3, F4), so the driver cannot claim any waiting-fee or no-show compensation from this trip (NS-1, NS-6) — the best available outcome is that no penalty attaches to him, not that he is paid.

Traffic evidence is thin: F10 shows only band 3 (20–29 km/h) on Boon Lay Way and F11 records no incidents, so an RD-4 'reasonable cause' style justification for any delay is not independently corroborated and should not be over-argued.

points.response: Correct on the branch, but it is fatal to the fee, not to us: the rider's own cancellation at 18:25:30 is the rider-cancellation branch of NS-0, which sends the case to NS-4 — and NS-4 charges nothing for a cancellation inside 3 minutes.
Accepted and it is our case: the 2 min 30 s cancellation at F2 falls inside the NS-4 3-minute grace window, so the $6.61 at F5 is not chargeable.

Agreed that NS-1 (i)-(iii) fail (no 'I'm Here' at F4, null arrival at F3, closest approach 1806 m at F1); that means no fee has any driver-side basis at all, and under NS-2 the $6.61 must be refunded in full — we seek no flag_account against a clean driver record (F14).

We do not need the driver to be culpable: the driver's 'About 5 min, traffic' at F8 is contradicted by 1806 m remaining at cancellation (F1) with no incident on record (F11) and only band 3 on one road (F10), but the refund follows from NS-4 regardless of who was at fault.

We agree no account action is warranted against the driver and expressly withdraw any flag_account request; F14 (0 disputes upheld in 604 days) supports that, and NS-2's flag attaches only where 'I'm Here' was pressed while outside the radius, which the null at F4 excludes.

The fee cannot be sustained, so the disposition is the opposite of no_action: with the cancellation inside the NS-4 grace window (F2) and no NS-1 condition met (F1, F3, F4), the $6.61 charged at F5 — with no surge to adjust (F6) — is refunded in full.

Accepted — the system timeline confirms the rider cancelled at 18:25:30, 2 min 30 s after acceptance at 18:23:00, so the fee is not chargeable against her under NS-4; my position is that the same facts also mean the fee was never a driver no-show penalty, so nothing should attach to the driver's account either.

Agreed on the finding, but the rider's framing is wrong: F1 (closest approach 1806 m, never within 200 m) and F3 (driver_arrived_at null) defeat the rider-cancellation no-show branch under NS-1/NS-2, which is a rule that protects the rider from an unjustified charge — it does not create any driver fault, and no NS-1 condition was ever triggered.

Conceded as to the fact: F4 shows the driver never tapped 'I'm Here', so no NS-1 cancellation or NS-6 waiting fee can ever be founded on this trip — which also means the driver seeks no fee from the rider, only that no adverse record be entered against him.

Not contested on amount: the record shows $6.61 charged and a 1.0× surge multiplier (F5, F6), so any refund is purely of the cancellation fee with no surcharge component — my revised outcome aligns with the rider's requested full refund of that fee rather than protecting it.

This point cuts both ways and the rider should read it carefully: F9 (driver: 'I was on my way when the rider cancelled') is consistent with F1 showing him still 1806 m away, i.e. moving but not yet arrived — F1/F3 are system records and they establish absence from the pickup point, not any dishonest statement or misconduct by the driver.

The traffic evidence (F10 only band 3, 20–29 km/h on Boon Lay Way; F11 no incidents; F12 fair weather) does not excuse any delay at the pickup point, and the driver does not need it to: NS-1 (i)–(iii) were never satisfied (F3, F4, F1), so no fee hangs on whether the driver was justified — and no ETA-lateness rule exists in Ryde's published policy.

Accepted as the correct treatment of profile data: F13 and F14 are context only and cannot decide this case; F14 (604-day account, 4.9 rating, 777 trips in 90 days, 0 disputes upheld) additionally means there is no repeated-violation pattern that could support any account action against the driver under RD-6.

notices.text: You cancelled about two and a half minutes after a driver accepted your ride, and that is inside the three-minute window where no cancellation fee applies. So we are refunding the $6.61 you were charged in full, paid as a Ryde voucher on your account. Nothing about your account changes because of this case. The driver's side was also checked: he never marked himself as arrived at the pickup point and was never recorded near it, which also points to a refund. You do not need to do anything further.

This trip's cancellation fee went back to the rider in full. The reason is timing: the rider cancelled about two and a half minutes after you accepted, inside the three-minute window where the fee is not chargeable, so the $6.61 could not stand. Separately, our records never showed you pressing "I'm Here" or being at the pickup point, so there was no arrival record to support keeping the fee. This is not a mark against you: no account action is being taken, and your rating and standing are unaffected.
